disease_label_per_paper: Left renal abscess requiring transgastric endoscopic drainage
presentation_summary: 30-year-old transgender male with asthma and history of kidney stone presented with several days of left flank pain after an outside CTA had shown a 4 cm left kidney mass versus abscess.
He reported fevers and chills at home but denied dysuria, hematuria, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and intravenous drug use.
Physical examination was notable for mild left flank tenderness; he was tachycardic but afebrile with otherwise stable vital signs.
Initial emergency-department labs showed WBC 17 x 10^9/L, absolute neutrophils 12.9 x 10^9/L, lactate 0.6, and creatinine 0.94 mg/dL.
Urinalysis showed pyuria 30-40 WBC/HPF, 3-5 RBC/HPF, small leukocyte esterase, negative nitrites, few bacteria, and trace protein.
CT abdomen with and without contrast showed a 4.1 x 4.1 x 3.8 cm rim-enhancing low-attenuation focus in the upper pole of the left kidney, consistent with renal abscess versus infected renal cyst.

imaging.source_text_value: CT of the abdomen with and without contrast demonstrated a 4.1 x 4.1 x 3.8 cm rim-enhancing low-attenuation focus involving the upper pole of the left kidney consistent with renal abscess versus infected renal cyst

microbiology.result: No growth from two separately drawn blood cultures
microbiology.source_text_value: Two separately drawn blood cultures returned negative
By postoperative day two, the abscess culture returned positive for scant Escherichia coli
Pleural fluid cultures after patient discharge grew Cutibacterium acnes

procedures.source_text_value: Percutaneous drain placement was attempted by IR twice but was unsuccessful due to location near diaphragm, pleura, and spleen
5 ccs purulent material aspirated; 7 French by 3 cm double-pigtail plastic stent placed into the left renal abscess creating a gastrorenal stent
stent removed after imaging showed decompression; tract closed with hemoclips and no extravasation
chest Pleurx catheter placed for left-sided pleural effusion with significant drainage

clinical_course.event: Started ceftriaxone; persistent flank pain despite supportive therapy led to urology, infectious disease, and interventional radiology consultation.
Switched to IV piperacillin-tazobactam to cover intra-abdominal infection because transgastric approach was planned.
Developed severe left upper quadrant and shoulder pain; CT showed stent in place but bilateral atelectasis, mediastinitis-suggestive findings, and transdiaphragmatic stent course.
Abscess culture grew scant E. coli; imaging showed significant decompression; stent removed due to discomfort.
Bilateral pneumonia, atelectasis, and left pleural effusion were diagnosed; leukocytosis improved but mild hypoxia persisted.
Leukocytosis continued to downtrend, respirations improved, chest drainage became minimal, and the patient clinically improved significantly.

actual_treatment: outside ceftriaxone and ketorolac before current presentation
Pleurx catheter drainage of pleural effusion

outcome.source_text_value: clinically improved significantly and was discharged home with ciprofloxacin and repeat CT follow-up

quality_warnings: Culture, organism, drainage procedure, complications, and response are preserved with use_in_ranking=false.
The presentation CT differential included infected renal cyst; this is retained in source_text_value rather than turned into a hard diagnosis label.
No exact heart rate or temperature was reported for the current emergency department visit; tachycardia and afebrile status are kept in narrative rather than assigned numeric vitals.
